source_links_enforced_means: The flag asserts that every MEASURED cell records all five mandated source layers with a date on each check; that a layer recorded as found carries what it yielded and a link resolving to that row's own trial identifier; and that a layer recorded as not available carries a reason and a date. title: Sotagliflozin against placebo across its pivotal cardiovascular outcome programme: three separate estimands, never merged -- two pooled within themselves, one reported from a single trial
question: In both phase 3 trials that supported sotagliflozin's approval, what is the effect of sotagliflozin compared with placebo on cardiovascular death and worsening heart failure -- counted as total events, counted as time to a first event, and on the three-component atherothrombotic endpoint -- with each of those questions answered separately?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the validator's numeric list. Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every measured input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from and a resolvable link to the layer it was read from. Every cell records all five mandated source layers with a date, so a layer that held nothing is distinguishable from a layer nobody opened. Derived transforms are computed here and are not claimed to appear in any source.
_estimand_rule: THE LABEL ON THE QUANTITY IS NOT THE QUANTITY. Both trials' primary endpoints are RECURRENT-EVENT analyses counting first and subsequent events, and the journal, the registry and the regulator all report them as hazard ratios. This object files them by what the analysis did. It holds three estimands and pools across none of them; within them, the two that both trials report are pooled, and the third -- reported by a single trial -- is not pooled at all. No automated effect-measure check in this repository could enforce that -- which is why the separation is structural rather than a warning.
single_tier_because: The primary tier is NOT uniform in this object and that is worth stating, because it is unusual here: the two total-occurrence outcomes are sourced to the primary publications, while every cell of the time-to-first outcome is sourced to the FDA statistical review, because that review is the only staged layer on earth that prints those numbers. A cell's tier follows where its value actually came from.
completeness_statement: FULL BUILD over a NAMED PROGRAMME, with the boundary stated. Both phase 3 cardiovascular outcome trials of this drug are held and each contributes to every estimand it reports. There is exactly ONE source list, `screening.records`; `screening.excluded` is a view COMPUTED from it at build time, row for row, so it cannot say anything the records do not. What is NOT claimed is a systematic database search: the scope is the pivotal programme as the regulator's own review defines it, and the prior-synthesis search that WAS run is recorded with its terms, its results and its date in a staged file.

verification_basis.what_verifies_this_object: Two things, and neither is a badge this repository can emit about itself. The object is the single source of truth and the page is a pure projection of it, so a claim on the page that is not in the object cannot exist. And the object is read by two model families with independent file access, from different vendors, each asked to find a defect in the ACTUAL object rather than to approve it.
verification_basis.what_is_not_claimed: No internal check is described as independent verification. A script that reads this object and reports it consistent has confirmed consistency and nothing else. Note also what this object could NOT get: no published synthesis reports either trial's own primary as a separate row, so no independent re-analysis checks these values.
verification_basis.bar: Both families must find no defect in the object. A finding about the validator is not a finding about the object and does not block.

regulator_ema.reason: The European regulator holds nothing for this outcome, and the reason is a fact about the INDICATION rather than about the agency's silence. Sotagliflozin WAS authorised in the European Union, on 26 April 2019, as Zynquista -- but as an adjunct to insulin therapy in adults with INSULIN-DEPENDENT DIABETES MELLITUS, which is the indication the staged medicine overview names in the regulator's own words, and the medicine overview staged here does not contain the phrase heart failure at all. That authorisation was withdrawn by the European Commission on 22 March 2022 at the marketing authorisation holder's request, for commercial reasons, which the staged public statement says in those words. What follows from those two documents is ONLY this: the European authorisation that existed was for another indication, and it no longer exists, so there is no European assessment of THIS endpoint to check against. An earlier version of this field went further and said a heart-failure indication had never been APPLIED FOR in Europe. Nothing staged here supports that -- the absence of a phrase from a medicine overview is not evidence that no application was ever filed -- and a gate leg was right to separate the claim the documents carry from the stronger one they do not. Both documents were read on the date recorded here rather than inferred from the absence of a link.

prior_meta.reason: A drug-specific prior synthesis EXISTS and is staged: a meta-analysis of sotagliflozin in diabetic populations covering nine studies. It does not yield this cell, and the reason is a difference of quantity rather than of availability -- it pools RELATIVE RISKS of heart failure events and of a composite cardiovascular endpoint -- each of those two analyses drawn from eight of its nine selected studies, not from all of them -- and restates neither trial's own primary as a separate row. Its abstract does not name its included trials, so its study list cannot be read from what is open either. An earlier version of this field said no synthesis could be LOCATED, which was too strong and was corrected after a gate leg found this paper in one step; the layer is unavailable for this cell, not unsearched, and the difference matters. Two class-level network meta-analyses were also fetched and read and name neither trial in their abstracts. Every query, with its date and its outcome, is staged beside this object.

divergences.note: This is a REAL cross-layer divergence and it is recorded rather than resolved. The publication and the registry agree with each other EXACTLY, to every digit. The FDA documents differ. No layer is corrected against another and no midpoint is invented: the cell stores what the two agreeing layers print, the regulator's figure is recorded here beside it, and a reader can see both. Nothing in the staged sources explains the difference, and this object does not guess at one -- the review describes its analyses as based on investigator-reported events in all randomized patients, which is a plausible starting point for an explanation but is not a statement that it accounts for this.

cascade.agreement_note: Publication and registry agree to every digit, including the denominators. The regulator layers agree on the point estimate and the upper bound and differ on the lower bound, which is recorded above.
cascade.primary_not_best_because: The FDA layer outranks the publication in this cascade's preference order and it DID hold this cell, so this key is required. It is not taken as the primary source because it is the layer that DISAGREES with the other two on the interval. Promoting a lone divergent layer over two that agree would resolve a divergence by ranking rather than by evidence, and the divergence is the finding here -- it is recorded on this cell precisely so that no reader has to take this object's word for which layer is right.

handbook.decision: POOL the two pivotal trials on THIS estimand alone, producing a drug-wide average across two documented population differences, and combine it with NO other estimand in this object
handbook.conformance: Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.3 fix the axes on which ELIGIBILITY turns -- population and comparator. Section 3.2.4 is cited for the caution it gives AGAINST making eligibility depend on which outcomes a study reported, which is why this object carries three outcomes rather than admitting only the trials that report one of them. Section 10.3 gives the METHOD -- log ratios combined by generic inverse variance -- and is the authority for combining WITHIN each estimand. What licenses the refusal to combine ACROSS them is that the estimands fall under DIFFERENT sections: a composite counting first and subsequent events is governed by 10.8, on counts and rates, while a time-to-first analysis is governed by 10.9. An earlier version cited 10.9 for both and for the method as well, which made the object commit in its own citations the conflation it exists to refuse. Section 10.10.1 is what distinguishes clinical and methodological diversity from statistical heterogeneity, which is why the uniformity table sits beside the statistic rather than being replaced by it -- with two trials the statistic is nearly powerless and the population difference it cannot see is the largest thing about this pool. Section 10.10.4 governs the model and the between-study variance estimator, 10.10.4.4 records restricted maximum likelihood as the current default, and 10.10.4.5 is why a more conservative interval is reported beside the ordinary one at this number of studies. Section 10.14 is the authority for the sensitivity analyses.

comparator: Both randomised against a matching placebo on top of background therapy.

population: This is the axis the pool crosses and it is the largest thing it crosses. One trial enrolled patients hospitalised for worsening heart failure and started treatment around discharge. The other enrolled patients with chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular risk in whom heart failure was NOT an entry requirement, and most did not have it. The pooled value is therefore a DRUG-WIDE estimate across the pivotal programme, which is the question this object asks, and it is not an estimate for a heart-failure population. The heart-failure-only result is the first trial's own row and a reader who wants it should read that row rather than the pool.
why_stopped: Both trials were terminated early because the sponsor withdrew funding. That is not a data-dependent stopping rule and it is not a boundary crossing; it is a commercial event, and it applies to both. What it cost was INFORMATION -- power and follow-up -- so it is carried into the GRADE IMPRECISION domain, where an unmet optimal information size is the ground for that downgrade. It is NOT carried into risk of bias: lost information widens an interval rather than biasing it. An earlier version of this row said the opposite and contradicted the risk-of-bias domain it was describing.
follow_up_length: Medians of about nine and about sixteen months. Each trial's own median is stored on its cell.
analysis_population: All randomised patients in both, with the registry posting the same two denominators on every outcome.
endpoint_rank_within_its_own_trial: This composite is the PRIMARY endpoint of both trials as they were finally analysed. In one of them it BECAME the primary by a change made during the trial, which the trial's own abstract states and which this object records on the cell and in the risk-of-bias domain rather than in a footnote.
ascertainment: Both trials' primary analyses rest on investigator-reported events, which the regulator's review states in those words. Centrally adjudicated versions of this endpoint DO exist for both trials in that review, and this outcome does NOT pool them: the parallel-ascertainment pool lives on the first-event estimand only, where both bases are printed in one regulator sentence. Here the contributing cells come from the publication and the registry on an investigator-reported basis, and building a second pool from a layer the cells are not drawn from would be a different synthesis wearing this one's name. An earlier version of this row said the adjudicated versions were reported in THIS outcome's sensitivity block; they are not, and a review leg was right that the prose claimed a feature the structure denies.

heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: UNDECIDABLE from this object. I-squared is 0 and Q is below the degrees of freedom, where the Higgins form is negative-and-clamped and the REML/metafor form is exactly zero -- BOTH DEFINITIONS GIVE 0 and nothing here distinguishes them. Recorded as undecidable rather than guessed.

hfcv_total.heterogeneity_status: Computed from Q and its single degree of freedom. With TWO studies this statistic has almost no power to detect heterogeneity, so a low value is consistent both with agreement and with not being able to tell, and it is reported with that caveat rather than as reassurance. The difference these two trials genuinely have is in their POPULATIONS, and no statistic computed from two effect estimates can see it -- the uniformity table is the only place it is visible.

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, a comparison of between-study variance estimators, and -- on the first-event estimand -- a parallel pool of the centrally adjudicated ascertainment
sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.14 for sensitivity analyses generally. Section 10.10.4.4 governs the estimator half: it records that methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better and that restricted maximum likelihood is the current default. Section 10.10.4.5 is cited for the INTERVAL comparison and not for the estimator comparison; it concerns interpretation with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval.
sensitivity.decision_under_test: Whether the pooled estimate depends on either single trial, on the choice of between-study variance estimator and interval method, and -- where two ascertainment bases exist -- on which of them is used.
sensitivity.leave_one_out_finding: With two trials a leave-one-out fit IS the other trial, and this table says so rather than presenting single-trial rows as though they were pooled sensitivity results. Read it as what it is: the two trials' own estimates, side by side, with the interval each carries alone.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: Section 10.10.4.4 records restricted maximum likelihood as the current default and that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better; that is the whole of the authority for running this comparison. Nothing in the Handbook instructs a review to run it at a particular number of studies, and running it here is a choice made under 10.14 because with two trials the choice is plausibly influential.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: Restricted maximum likelihood with the ordinary interval, because section 10.10.4.4 records it as the current default and as a better estimator than DerSimonian and Laird. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is reported beside it with the floor on its scale factor applied, so it can widen and can never come out narrower than the ordinary one. It is NOT presented as the interval to prefer: section 10.10.4.5 says the opposite is possible, that with only two or three studies such intervals can be EXCESSIVELY WIDE and an ordinary interval may be preferable, and it asks for the comparison rather than for a winner. An earlier version of this field called it the interval to weigh most heavily, which attributed to that section a preference it does not express.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: Reported as computed rather than summarised in advance. Where the estimators agree it is because there is little between-study variance for them to disagree about, which at two studies is close to uninformative; where the conservative interval is much wider than the ordinary one, that width is the honest expression of how little two trials constrain a random-effects average, and section 10.10.4.5 says to expect it.

risk_of_bias.basis_in_sources: BOTH trials were terminated early because the sponsor withdrew funding, and THIS DOMAIN DOES NOT REST ON THAT. The usual stopped-early reasoning does not apply here: the danger with a trial stopped early FOR BENEFIT is an inflated effect at a data-dependent boundary, and the stop here was commercial, so there was no boundary to stop at. The early termination is named in this domain because any reader will look for it, and it is then explicitly SET ASIDE as a ground for it. An earlier version of this field said the object 'treats that as serious' and then argued in the next clause that it introduces no bias, which is a contradiction a gate leg was right to refuse. What carries the SERIOUS rating is internal validity alone: BOTH trials changed their primary objectives during the trials, and both rest their primary analysis on investigator-reported rather than centrally adjudicated events. The lost power and lost follow-up that early termination also caused are NOT counted here -- they widen intervals rather than bias them, so they belong to imprecision, and an earlier version of this domain double-counted them. A gate leg was right that downgrading risk of bias for lost power is a misapplication of the domains. The endpoint change is the most serious of the three: it is exactly the condition that outcome-reporting-bias guidance is about, and it is recorded on the trial, on the cell and here.

inconsistency.derived_from: Q against its degrees of freedom and the between-study variance, both stored in this result's heterogeneity block. Section 14.2.2 makes the trigger unexplained heterogeneity rather than a value of the statistic, and the one large clinical difference between these trials -- their populations -- is documented in the uniformity table rather than offered as a post-hoc explanation. indirectness.basis_in_sources: Not downgraded, and the reasoning is worth stating because the opposite call is tempting. The frozen question is the drug across its PIVOTAL PROGRAMME, and the evidence is exactly that programme: the population, the intervention, the comparator and the outcomes are the ones the question names, measured in the trials themselves. The population SPREAD between the trials is real and large, but it is diversity WITHIN the question rather than a mismatch between the question and the evidence, and section 10.10.1 is where it belongs -- the uniformity table -- not here. An earlier version of this domain downgraded on the ground that a reader wanting a heart-failure answer would misread the pooled value. That is a risk of MISREADING, answered by labelling and by the scope block, and downgrading for it would be stricter than the Handbook while claiming the Handbook's support -- the same defect a gate leg caught on the companion review in this batch.

imprecision.triggers_computed: Condition one, the ordinary interval excluding the null: MET on every outcome here. Condition three, the optimal information size: NOT MET and not merely uncomputable -- both trials were terminated before they collected the information they were designed for, so whatever the target was, it was not reached. imprecision.derived_from: The pooled interval stored in this result, and the alternative-method interval reported beside it in the sensitivity block. unresolved.item: no independent synthesis checks the values in this object
unresolved.detail: Four dated queries found no synthesis reporting either trial's own primary endpoint as a separate row, and the closest class-level network meta-analyses do not name either trial in their abstracts, so their included-study lists cannot be read from what is open. The consequence is stated plainly rather than minimised: the per-cell values here rest on the publication, the registry and the regulator, and on no independent re-analysis. A synthesis may exist behind a paywall or under indexing these queries did not reach.

Both total-occurrence cells differ between the FDA documents and the agreeing publication and registry -- on the lower bound for the smaller trial, on the point estimate for the larger. Within the FDA the two documents agree with each other on BOTH trials: an earlier version of this entry said they differed on the larger one, which was this object's own error and is corrected in the corrected-claims block. Nothing in the staged sources explains it. The review describes its analyses as based on investigator-reported events in all randomized patients, which is where an explanation would start, but the staged text does not say that it accounts for these differences and this object does not assert that it does.

claims_corrected.claim: that the worsening-heart-failure trial's time-to-first estimate is the value supplied to this build
claims_corrected.correction: The regulator's review reports two such estimates, one per ascertainment basis, and the supplied figure is neither. Its lower bound coincides with the lower bound of one of them, which is how a bound becomes an estimate in a chain of custody.

claims_corrected.claim: that the European application for this drug was withdrawn
claims_corrected.correction: An authorisation was granted and later withdrawn, and it was for insulin-dependent diabetes rather than heart failure. That is why the European layer holds nothing for this endpoint. What is NOT claimed, because the staged documents do not show it, is that a heart-failure indication was never applied for -- an overview that omits a phrase is not a record of what was never filed.

claims_corrected.claim: that this review can report one pooled effect for sotagliflozin
claims_corrected.correction: It holds three estimands and pools none of them together. The trials' own primary is a total-occurrence analysis reported as a hazard ratio; the time-to-first analysis of the same composite is a different set of numbers held only by the regulator; and the three-component first-occurrence endpoint is reported by one trial. A single headline would have to merge at least two of those.

claims_corrected.claim: that the two FDA documents disagree with each other about the larger trial's total-occurrence primary endpoint
claims_corrected.correction: They agree to every digit. The review's PRIMARY endpoint analysis and the label's efficacy table print the same interval, and the differing lower bound this object had quoted from the review belongs to a SENSITIVITY analysis on the same endpoint -- the one censoring non-cardiovascular deaths as non-informative. A value was matched across documents without the ANALYSIS it belongs to, which is the defect this object's own cascade exists to prevent, committed by the object itself and built into a headline before a gate leg caught it. The surviving divergence is real and unchanged: the publication and the registry print a different point estimate from the one both FDA documents print. The companion trial was re-checked the same way and needed no correction -- there the review's primary line and the label's table do print the interval this object records.

SCOPE:three-estimands-never-merged.decision: The total-occurrence composite, the time-to-first analysis of that same composite, and the three-component first-occurrence endpoint are three separate outcomes, each with its own result block and its own certainty rating, and no value crosses between them. TWO of them are pooled; the third is reported by a single trial and is not pooled at all, which its own result block says on its face. An earlier version of this sentence claimed three separate POOLS, which implied a synthesis for that third outcome that the sources do not support and that the structured result correctly refuses.
SCOPE:three-estimands-never-merged.conformance: Section 10.9 fixes what may be combined: log hazard ratios for the same quantity by generic inverse variance. A proportional-rates analysis over first and subsequent events and a Cox analysis of the time to a first event are not the same quantity, and every layer here calls both of them a hazard ratio -- which is precisely why the separation has to be structural rather than a note. Section 3.2.4 is why all three are carried instead of only the one the trials designated primary.

SCOPE:the-label-on-the-quantity-is-not-t.decision: A value is filed by what the analysis DID, never by what the source called it. Both trials' primary endpoints are recurrent-event analyses reported as hazard ratios by the journal, the registry and the regulator alike, and they are filed as total-occurrence estimands.
SCOPE:the-label-on-the-quantity-is-not-t.conformance: This is the single most load-bearing decision in the object and the one no automated check in this repository could make for it: an effect-measure detector sees two hazard ratios and is satisfied. The companion review in this batch EXCLUDED one of these very trials for this reason. This object includes it and separates the estimands instead, which is a different answer to the same fact and is defensible only because the separation is structural.

SCOPE:publication-two-component-first-ev.decision: The larger trial's publication reports a first-occurrence composite of cardiovascular death OR hospitalization for heart failure -- TWO components, without urgent heart failure visits. This object does not use it for the time-to-first estimand and stores no value from it. The time-to-first estimand here is the time-to-first analysis of that trial's OWN primary composite, which has three components, and the regulator's review is the only staged layer that prints it. Treating the publication's two-component figure as the same cell would put a different event set under the same name -- the conflation this object exists to refuse -- and it would also re-source a load-bearing row to a layer that does not print it.
SCOPE:publication-two-component-first-ev.conformance: Section 3.2.4 governs which outcomes a review defines and how they are grouped. A composite is defined by its event set, so two composites differing in a component are two outcomes and not two labels for one. Section 10.9 governs the time-to-event analysis the two share, which is exactly why the shared analysis type is not sufficient to make them one cell. This block exists because an earlier version of the time-to-first cascade cell said this composite was 'recorded in the screening and scope blocks rather than silently used here' when it was recorded in NEITHER -- a cross-reference that pointed at nothing. A gate leg found it; this block is the record the sentence claimed.

SCOPE:drug-wide-pivotal-not-heart-failur.decision: The question is the drug across its pivotal programme, so both trials are in and the pooled value spans a heart-failure population and a diabetes-and-kidney-disease population. The heart-failure-only result is a labelled SUBGROUP -- one trial's own row -- and never the headline.
SCOPE:drug-wide-pivotal-not-heart-failur.conformance: Section 3.2.1 makes the population a defining criterion, and this object defines it as the pivotal programme rather than as a disease. That is a legitimate question and it is also the one most open to being misread, so the population difference is the largest row in every uniformity table here. It is deliberately NOT a reason to downgrade indirectness: the frozen question IS the drug-wide programme, so the spread is diversity WITHIN the question rather than a mismatch with it, and it is carried under section 10.10.1 in the uniformity table instead. An earlier version of this sentence said the indirectness domain was downgraded for it, which contradicted the GRADE blocks themselves; a gate leg found the contradiction by reading both.

SCOPE:no-number-needed-to-treat.decision: No absolute risk reduction and no number needed to treat is computed or displayed anywhere in this object, on any outcome.
SCOPE:no-number-needed-to-treat.conformance: On the total-occurrence outcome the arithmetic is not merely unhelpful, it has no meaning in the usual sense: the denominator of a number needed to treat is a difference in the PROPORTION of people with an event, and this endpoint counts events rather than people. On the other two outcomes it would need an assumed control risk over a stated horizon that no field here carries. The renderer computes none, which was checked rather than assumed.

published_comparison._why: This review pools two trials on a total-occurrence composite reported as a hazard ratio. The question a reader needs answered is whether the published literature reports that quantity, and whether anyone -- them or us -- got it wrong. Both halves are reported below, with the number of records screened.
published_comparison._how_identified: PubMed E-utilities, query and counts recorded in ssot/sotagliflozin-hf/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json, which carries a decision for every record. This layer is machine-screened at ABSTRACT level and the limitation is stated there and in the checks below.

checks.what: An unexplained precision gap in the drug-specific meta-analysis
checks.detail: Its printed interval 0.64 to 0.69 implies a standard error on the log scale of about 0.0192; our two-trial pool over 11,806 participants implies 0.0705. With 8,040 and 7,280 participants, an event in 10% of each arm gives 0.0485, 20% gives 0.0324, and even 30% in both arms gives 0.0247 -- all wider than printed. THE STRONGEST INNOCENT EXPLANATION IS PLAUSIBLE AND IS STATED: if the pool counts total recurrent events rather than participants, counts can exceed the participant number and that precision is attainable. The abstract does not state the unit of analysis, so this is recorded for a reader and NOT asserted as an error. Full text or the PROSPERO record would settle it.

divergence_decomposed.ours: HR 0.7171 (0.6246 to 0.8234) for the total number of occurrences of CV death, HF hospitalisation and urgent HF visit, k=2, both pivotal trials.
divergence_decomposed.theirs: RR 0.66 (0.64 to 0.69) for heart failure over 8 studies, and RR 0.73 (0.66 to 0.81) for MACE over 8 studies.
divergence_decomposed.why_they_differ: A different quantity (a relative risk of experiencing an event is not a hazard ratio for the total number of events), a different eligible set (nine mixed-design studies against the two pivotal trials), and a different question. Same direction, but direction agreement is worth little across estimands: a close answer to a different question is the most persuasive kind of wrong. NEITHER SIDE IS SHOWN TO BE IN ERROR HERE, and that is the finding.

risk_of_bias.tool: RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials)
risk_of_bias.version: 22 August 2019 version, as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook
risk_of_bias.handbook: Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5, 2024.
risk_of_bias.unit_of_assessment: A RESULT, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: risk of bias is assessed for a specific result. The same trial is assessed TWICE here and lands differently: SOLOIST-WHF's total-event result is its registered primary and its first-event result was never registered at all. A study-level rating would have averaged those two into one number and lost the only distinction this assessment actually makes.
risk_of_bias.default_rule: A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never SOME_CONCERNS. A rating of SOME CONCERNS with no explanation reads as a judgement against the trial, and neither of these trials has done anything to earn one.
risk_of_bias.what_this_assessment_could_actually_deci: ONE DOMAIN OF FIVE, and it is worth saying plainly rather than burying in the table. Domain 5 is judged from evidence -- the full registered outcome list for both trials, read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18, which Handbook 8.7 names as the method for this domain. Domains 1 to 3 are NO_INFORMATION on all four results. Domain 4 is judged on one result of four, and only because this object happens to hold the same estimand measured a second way.

ceiling.statement: NO RESULT IN THIS REVIEW CAN REACH LOW RISK OF BIAS ON THE EVIDENCE WE CAN REACH, because domains 1 to 3 are NO_INFORMATION on all four results. That is a limit of this review's retrieval, not a finding about SOLOIST-WHF or SCORED, both of which are large double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trials.
ceiling.what_would_change_it: Retrieving each trial's full published report with its supplementary appendix, and its protocol and statistical analysis plan. Those answer the signalling questions for domains 1 to 3 directly. For SCORED, the protocol history would also settle whether the mid-trial endpoint change was made blind to accumulating results -- which is the single fact that would move domain 5 off HIGH on two of the four results.
ceiling.why_stated_rather_than_left_implicit: A ceiling that is not stated looks like a verdict. A reader who sees three of five domains unjudged and no explanation will read the overall rating as a criticism of the trials, and it is not one.

D5_selection_of_reported_result.reason: THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT WAS CHANGED DURING THE TRIAL, and this object carries the sentence verbatim: 'The primary end point was changed during the trial to the composite of the total number of deaths from cardiovascular causes, hospitalizations for heart failure...'. The estimand this pool uses IS the changed endpoint. Handbook 8.7 covers bias arising when 'the reported result is selected (based on its direction, magnitude or statistical significance) from among multiple intervention effect estimates'; a mid-trial change of the primary is that situation at its clearest, and nothing available to us establishes that the change was made blind to accumulating results. Rated HIGH. NOT EXCLUDED: Handbook chapter 3 makes registration status no part of eligibility, and this corpus settled the same question on 2026-08-18 for ANSWER-HF, deciding that an endpoint problem is graded rather than used to remove a trial -- because a wrong exclusion publishes a result we created, while a wrong inclusion leaves the evidence intact.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In both phase 3 trials that supported sotagliflozin's approval, what is the effect of sotagliflozin compared with placebo on cardiovascular death and worsening heart failure -- counted as total events, counted as time to a first event, and on the three-component atherothrombotic endpoint -- with each of those questions answered separately?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against placebo on top of background therapy.

The outcomes pooled are Total occurrences of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure and urgent heart failure visit, as a hazard ratio; Time to the FIRST occurrence of that same composite, as a hazard ratio. One further outcome is reported without pooling: Time to the first occurrence of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or non-fatal stroke, as a hazard ratio, and the reason is recorded with it.

endpoint_history_correction_2026_08_26._what: A correction to this object's description of the two trials' endpoint history. It corrects a DESCRIPTION and re-rates nothing.
endpoint_history_correction_2026_08_26.what_this_object_said: That SCORED changed its primary endpoint during the trial, with no corresponding statement about SOLOIST-WHF. Stated in that one-sided form in at least eight fields, including the GRADE risk-of-bias basis on three outcomes.
endpoint_history_correction_2026_08_26.what_is_true: BOTH programmes changed their primary objectives during the trials. The shift was from time-to-event analyses of ADJUDICATED events to TOTAL (first and potentially subsequent) INVESTIGATOR-REPORTED events, and the FDA reviewer records it as pre-specified.

quotes: While there was a major change to the primary objectives for SOLOIST and SCORED, the Applicant's pre-specified plan to shift from time-to-event analyses of adjudicated events to total (first and potentially subsequent) investigator-reported events was reasonable and is sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness.
SOLOIST was originally planned to assess a time-to-event analysis for first and recurrent CV death, HHF and UHFV events.

endpoint_history_correction_2026_08_26.what_this_does_NOT_change: Two things. First, no rating moves: the risk-of-bias assessment on this object is unadjudicated and every certainty rating is PENDING, and a corrected trial history is an input to that adjudication rather than a reason to re-rate tonight. Second, the claim that NEITHER TRIAL REGISTERED a time-to-first-event analysis remains true and is not withdrawn -- both registry records post the amended total-occurrence primary. Registered is not the same as planned.
endpoint_history_correction_2026_08_26.bearing_on_the_pending_adjudication: The FDA reviewer describes the change as PRE-SPECIFIED and notes a sensitivity analysis of the original time-to-event strategy. A change made before database lock and unblinding is not automatically high risk of bias under RoB 2 domain 5. Both assessors judged D5 without this fact in front of them, and their recorded reasoning is left untouched here so the adjudicator can see what each reader actually had.
endpoint_history_correction_2026_08_26.unresolved: The external review states SOLOIST's original primary was time to first CV death or HF hospitalisation with the recurrent three-component composite secondary. The source held here says the original plan was a time-to-event analysis for first AND recurrent CV death, HHF and UHFV. This object holds neither the original protocol nor the final SAP, so the two accounts are recorded side by side rather than one being chosen.
